analysis: Distribution on four key sets of about 65,536 keys (random strings, decimal 0..65535, near-duplicates, synthetic words). Every reverse-pass QG variant fails on the three structured sets (chi-square z up to 26,000 with 1024 buckets, 2.4-2.7 times the expected bucket collisions, 32,624 full 64-bit collisions on near-duplicates) - exactly as the tail-information bound predicts; the 2-pass forward hash passes the chi-square tests but has 723 full collisions on near-duplicates. MX64 and BLAKE2b pass everything; FNV-1a and CRC32 fail mildly on sequential and near-duplicate keys (z = -9.8 and -20.5 for sequential keys). A first run failed (synthetic words passed as str instead of bytes) and was fixed; the corrected META key count (65,280 near-duplicates) reproduced the same result hash.
assumptions: key sets (seeded): 65536 random byte strings of length 4-32; the decimal strings of 0..65535; near-duplicates = 16 random 16-byte bases with all 4080 single-byte substitutions each (65280 keys); 65536 distinct synthetic pronounceable words (no dictionary file is available offline)
z = (chi2 - df)/sqrt(2 df); |z| > 3 is flagged; collisions counted among the low 16 bits
counterexamples: QG-NIMINV p2+rev: z = 1084 (1024 buckets) on the decimal strings 0..65535 and 32,624 full 64-bit collisions on near-duplicate keys (H-C18-3 refuted)
falsification: H-C18-3b: |z| > 3 or a collision ratio outside [0.98, 1.02] for NIMINV. H-C18-6: QG-ARP p1 within bounds on near-duplicates.

hypothesis: H-C18-3b (bold): the nimber inversion hash (QG-NIMINV p2+rev) has |chi-square z| <= 3 on every key set and bucket-collision ratio within 2% of the uniform expectation, like FNV-1a-64. H-C18-6: the 1-pass x + c(y) hash (QG-ARP p1) fails on near-duplicate keys.
methodology: Hash every key set with every variant; compute z-scores for 1024 buckets (low 10 bits) and 1021 buckets (h mod 1021); count keys landing in an occupied bucket among 2^16 (low 16 bits) and full 64-bit collisions.
question: Do quasigroup hashes distribute realistic key sets as evenly as standard hashes?
title: Hash-table behaviour: chi-square of bucket counts (1024 buckets by mask, 1021 by modulus) and collisions in 2^16 buckets on random, sequential, near-duplicate and word-like keys
